---
title: "Scaled Dot-Product Attention"
---

## Intuition

Attention computes a content-dependent weighted average of values.

## Derivation

Given query, key, and value matrices,

$$
Q \in \mathbb{R}^{n_q \times d}, \quad
K \in \mathbb{R}^{n_k \times d}, \quad
V \in \mathbb{R}^{n_k \times d_v},
$$

scaled dot-product attention is

$$
\operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)
=
\operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt d}\right)V.
$$

### Why divide by $\sqrt d$?

If the coordinates of $q$ and $k$ are approximately independent with unit variance, then

$$
\operatorname{Var}(q^T k) \approx d.
$$

Dividing by $\sqrt d$ keeps logits at an approximately constant scale as head dimension grows, avoiding increasingly saturated softmax outputs.

## Minimal PyTorch implementation

::: {#f50c659d .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import math
import torch


def attention(q, k, v, mask=None):
    scores = q @ k.transpose(-2, -1) / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1])

    if mask is not None:
        scores = scores.masked_fill(~mask, float("-inf"))

    weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    return weights @ v
```
:::

q = torch.randn(2, 4, 8)
